subject: Rerank model fit validation & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kevin Liu <kevin@searchly.com>
Cc: Emma Torres <emma@searchly.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Rerank model fit validation & next steps

Hi Kevin / Emma —

Thanks again for the call earlier today — good coverage on intent drift and the query distribution for your e-commerce vertical. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned on scope and success criteria for the rerank pilot.

Recap (from discovery)
- Primary goal: increase top-10 relevancy for query-based product search, measured by NDCG@10 and MRR.
- Current production baseline (internal): NDCG@10 = 0.542, MRR = 0.376 (derived from 10k labeled queries you described).
- Latency target: 95th < 120ms for rerank step in our pipelined inference.
- Label format: graded relevance 0/1/2 (we discussed).

Recommended offline evaluation plan (what Redwood will run)
1) Models to evaluate: rw-t5-re-rank-3b (fp16), rw-bert-rerank-1.3 (optimized), rw-mini-pt-rerank-q4 (quantized low-cost variant).
2) Metrics: NDCG@1/3/10, MRR, Recall@10, inference P95 latency, and unit-cost per 1k requests.
3) Datasets: please share the 10k labeled queries + click logs; we will hold 1k as a blind test set.
4) Prompt/feature sets: we'll run two prompt variants (sparse BM25 context + raw text; enriched with category/context tokens). See attached prompt_sets_v1.json for the exact prompt templates.
5) A/B plan (pilot): start with offline eval -> 2-week online A/B running 10% traffic for top candidate if offline shows >6% relative NDCG@10 uplift and MRR improvement > 0.03. Ramp to 50% if metrics are stable and latency SLOs met.

Preliminary offline results (internal quick pass)
- rw-t5-re-rank-3b: NDCG@10 = 0.601 (+10.9% vs baseline), MRR = 0.423 (+12.5%).
- rw-bert-rerank-1.3: NDCG@10 = 0.585 (+8.0%), MRR = 0.411 (+9.3%).
- rw-mini-pt-rerank-q4: NDCG@10 = 0.564 (+4.1%), MRR = 0.392 (+4.3%).
(See attached rerank_offline_results_ndcg_mrr.csv and ndcg_table.pdf for the full breakdown by query slice.)

Open questions / asks for you
- Can you provision read-only S3 access to the labeled dataset and clickstream container? (we'd like to pull the 10k bundle and run offline evals)
- Any restrictions on serving region (we recommended us-west clusters but can accommodate eu if needed)?
- Would Searchly be open to a 60-day pilot commitment? We can structure pricing for pilot credits; will ping Laura for approval if you want an explicit discount for the POC.

Next steps
- Kevin: share S3 link + sample label format (JSONL or CSV) — target Wed EOD PST.
- Redwood (Priyom/Ben): run full offline evaluation and deliver a one-pager with slice-level NDCG/MRR and latency/cost estimates by next Tue.
- If offline looks good: schedule 30-min sync to finalize A/B rollout and monitoring hooks.

Attachments: prompt_sets_v1.json (templates), rerank_offline_results_ndcg_mrr.csv (summary)

Thanks — looking forward to moving.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com

Kevin

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kevin Liu <kevin@searchly.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emma Torres <emma@searchly.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T18:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rerank model fit validation & next steps

Kevin — thanks for the S3 link, I confirmed read access and pulled a 1k sample. I ran a quick offline slice analysis and attached the ndcg_table.pdf with per-query-length and per-category breakdowns. Notes:

- The gains for rw-t5-re-rank-3b are concentrated on long-tail, multi-term queries (NDCG@10 uplift ~+18% there). For short branded queries the delta is smaller.
- Latency numbers (local benchmark): rw-t5-re-rank-3b baseline P95 = 98ms (on our dedicated us-west pod with batch size tuned), rw-bert-rerank-1.3 P95 = 64ms, rw-mini-pt-rerank-q4 P95 = 43ms. These are inference-only for the rerank call (excludes retrieval time).
- Cost estimate (rough): per-1k requests: rw-t5-re-rank-3b = $3.10, rw-bert-rerank-1.3 = $1.85, rw-mini-pt-rerank-q4 = $0.68. We'll provide a detailed cost/latency tradeoff matrix in the full deliverable.

Proposed validation steps (detailed)
1) Offline run: full 10k -> compute NDCG/MRR by slice, produce confidence intervals and per-query delta vs baseline.
2) Synthetic latency testing: run a replay of 1k qps traffic at 10% pilot load to validate P95 with realistic batching.
3) Online A/B: 10% traffic for 14 days with automatic rollback if NDCG@10 drops or if latency SLO is breached for 3 consecutive hours.

I'll kick off the offline run tonight and aim to share the full CSV + one-pager Tuesday morning. Ben — looping Laura for pilot pricing approval if Searchly wants a discounted POC rate.

Thanks,
Priyom
